lines.why: Fresh. Nothing aired wishes anyone a happy anything, and no aired line uses a themed week's name as a greeting. The nearest aired things are a monologue joke about two themed weeks falling on one day, and a sign-off in which the host at last said the community's own two-letter goodnight as the payoff of a runner. This line is neither: its premise is the week's name treated as a holiday, it pays off no runner, and the week it names is this window's own. One caution for later weeks: the cluster names a week most weeks, so 'Happy <name> week.' is a formula that will fit every close. Said a second time it is a sign-off, and the next reviewer should treat it as one.

Fresh. The owner has put a goodnight in the frame, so the two words themselves cannot be the test; what is tested is what else the line carries. Each aired goodnight carried a load: one ended on 'friends', as the answer to the question the night had asked; one was the two-letter goodnight addressed to the community by name, as a runner's payoff; and a sung one said what had been built. 'Good night, everybody.' carries none of those: no 'friends', no abbreviation, no community's name, no tally. It is the plainest form the frame allows. Had the address been the community's name, it would have been the aired sign-off. Two notes, neither a block. 'everybody' was the host's closing address in three aired buttons, the aired song's among them; that is how a host talks and not a phrase a viewer will recognise, but it is a tic if it ends lines again next week. And the same plain goodnight said two weeks running would become the fixed words the frame says a close must not have.

Fresh. A plain pointer forward: no aired line says what is left of the night by naming a segment to come. The aired lines nearest in job were a general promise of a great show with an instruction to stay, and a line near the end saying the show was almost over; this is neither, in words or in mechanism. It does not need last week: to a new viewer 'the song' means only that a song is coming. One caution: the definite article treats the song as a fixture the viewer expects, and a join that names 'the song' again next week would be a stock join.

inside: 'Happy polyhedra week.' picks up the one time the week is named aloud, a member's own 'polyhedron week comes in many forms' performed in the coffee segment, and works as a callback by a different character that still reads alone for a viewer who missed it; 'Good night, everybody.' echoes no spoken line, though the studio's credits then head themselves 'Good night, Bluesky', so the goodnight is said to one addressee and shown to another within seconds.
